one_sentence_story: At Yale in 1961, ordinary men were told to give a stranger bigger and bigger electric shocks for wrong answers, and 26 of 40 kept pressing switches all the way to 450 volts, even though the shocks were fake and the 'learner' was in on it.
so_what_for_you: When a respected place and a calm voice tell you that something harmful is 'for a good reason, please continue', you are in the exact situation that made good people go along; seeing the person affected, dropping the official setting, or one friend saying no makes it far easier to stop, and bare orders are the ones people resist most.
